headline: Simple Chewing Gum Cuts Cancer-Linked Virus by 93%
meta_description: University of Pennsylvania researchers developed chewing gum that reduces HPV levels by up to 93% while preserving healthy mouth bacteria.
summary_short: A specially engineered chewing gum reduced cancer-linked HPV by up to 93% in patient samples, offering hope for a safer, more affordable therapy.
body:
Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania have developed a bioengineered chewing gum that dramatically reduces human papillomavirus and harmful bacteria associated with head and neck cancer. In tests using oral samples from patients, the gum reduced HPV levels by 93% in saliva and 80% in oral rinse samples. The treatment also nearly eliminated two dangerous bacterial species—*Porphyromonas gingivalis* and *Fusobacterium nucleatum*—while preserving the beneficial bacteria that normally protect the mouth. The findings, published in *Scientific Reports*, suggest a potentially accessible and affordable way to complement existing cancer therapies.

Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma remains one of the most serious cancers worldwide, ranked as the seventh leading cancer type in incidence and mortality among adolescents and young adults globally in 2022. Current medications have failed to dramatically improve survival rates or quality of life for many patients, creating an urgent need for new approaches. The gum is made from lablab beans and contains FRIL, a naturally occurring antiviral protein. Researchers then engineered it further to include protegrin, an antimicrobial peptide that targets dangerous bacteria. A single dose brought bacterial levels down to almost zero.

What sets this innovation apart is its gentleness. Unlike radiation therapy, which can destroy helpful mouth bacteria and encourage the growth of harmful yeast infections, this chewing gum selectively targets only dangerous microbes. The team believes the gum could eventually serve alongside current cancer treatments or help prevent infection and transmission in at-risk individuals. Henry Daniell, the lead researcher, emphasizes that advancing these findings toward clinical trials represents a meaningful opportunity to give patients additional tools in their fight against one of medicine's most stubborn challenges.
quick_facts: University of Pennsylvania researchers developed antiviral chewing gum
HPV levels reduced by up to 93% in patient samples
Made from lablab beans containing FRIL antiviral protein
Preserved beneficial mouth bacteria unlike radiation therapy
Findings published August 2026 in Scientific Reports
